title: Non-Torque Loading System for Electrical Machine Testing Including Drive System
description: The University of Edinburgh seeks to acquire a Non-Torque Loading System with a minimum power rating of 20 kW and preferably up to 50 kW or above. The system should be capable of applying non-torque loads to the shaft/rotor of the motor/generator under test of at least 50 kN in at least 2-axes, but preferably 3-axes. It should also have a speed range of at least 20-100 rpm, but preferably up to 10-1000 rpm. Preference is for electrically actuated non-torque loading. Our researchers design, develop and test small electrical machines (at full scale), as well as downscaled prototypes of electrical machines for large offshore renewable energy applications.

The Service Provider shall be a member of, accredited by, or operate in accordance with the standards, codes of conduct and professional requirements of the Market Research Society (MRS) or an equivalent recognised professional body for market research, social research, insight or analytics. This Contract shall primarily provide Fieldwork Surveys and associated Project Management, Client Data Access, Analysis and Reporting for each of our four gallery sites. Services will be agreed to on an âas requiredâ basis with no commitment to a minimum volume of work. NGS may, at its absolute discretion, require the Service Provider to provide Audience Research Services at this fifth site, currently under construction, at any time during the Contract term. If permitted by applicable procurement legislation, where additional audience research requirements arise during the Contract term that constitute an extension of the Services, NGS reserves the right to procure such additional services from the Service Provider. For full details of the Contract Requirements please refer to the associated Tender and Contract Documents. The Service Provider must have a clear understanding of the contract requirements and the organisational needs of NGS. As part of the tender exercise, the Service Provider must detail a robust and flexible methodology for conducting Audience Research Services that will meet all data capture requirements. There is no commitment to a minimum spend over the duration of the Contract. Under this Contract, no minimum spend is guaranteed. The agreement will be non-exclusive i.e. NGS reserves the right, in certain, circumstances, to procure out with the Contract Agreement, as and when required. In the event of unsatisfactory performance by the successful Service Provider and the termination of the contract by either party, NGS reserves the right to negotiate the continuance of the services with the second and third placed Service Providers.

title: Mobile Firefighter Training Prop
description: REQUEST FOR QUOATES MOBILE FIREFIGHTER TRAINING PROP GENERAL INFORMATION This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products prepared in accordance with the format in FAR Subpart 12.6, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; quotations are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. This solicitation is issued as a Request for Quotation (RFQ). The solicitation document and incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through Federal Acquisition Circular (FAC) 2026-01. The Government intends to award a Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) contract/purchase order for one (1) mobile firefighter training prop meeting or exceeding the requirements identified in this solicitation. REQUIREMENT The Government requires one (1) compact, mobile, versatile firefighter training device designed for on-site use at a fire station. The training system shall provide firefighters with the ability to conduct realistic, repeatable training scenarios without requiring construction of permanent training infrastructure. The system shall be constructed from ruggedized, weather-resistant materials such as Corten steel, modified shipping-container construction, or equivalent materials capable of withstanding severe weather, intensive use, and physical impact associated with firefighter training. CLIN 0001 � Mobile Firefighter Training Prop Quantity: 1 Each Unit Price: $____________ Total Price: $____________ The quoted price shall include all materials, fabrication, equipment, accessories required to meet the minimum requirements, packaging, freight, and delivery to the Government-designated destination. MINIMUM TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS The proposed system shall meet or exceed all of the following minimum requirements: a. Integrated forcible-entry door prop suitable for repeated firefighter training. b. Adjustable-pitch roof simulator capable of supporting ventilation training. c. Second-story platform or structure capable of supporting ladder-placement, rescue, and elevated-access training. d. Internal and/or external training modules capable of supporting: Confined-space exercises; Wall-breach exercises; Entanglement exercises; and Related firefighter rescue and survival training. e. The system shall support a minimum of twenty (20) distinct, repeatable firefighter training scenarios. f. The system shall be constructed for exterior/on-site use and shall be sufficiently durable to withstand: Severe weather exposure; Intensive and recurring training; Physical impact from firefighting hand tools and equipment; and Normal wear associated with repeated firefighter training. g. The system shall be designed and constructed in accordance with applicable requirements of NFPA 1402, Standard on Facilities for Fire Training and Associated Props. h. Confined-space/rescue training capabilities shall be designed in accordance with applicable NFPA 1006 requirements. i. Guardrail systems shall meet or exceed applicable OSHA requirements, including OSHA 1926.502(b)(3). j. The system shall utilize modular, universal, or commercially available components wherever practicable to permit future upgrades or replacement. k. Consumable components used during training, including wooden blocks, dowels, or similar forcible-entry components, shall be replaceable using readily available commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) materials. TECHNICAL DOCUMENTATION Quoters shall provide sufficient technical information for the Government to determine whether the proposed product meets all minimum requirements. Technical documentation shall include, at a minimum: a. Product make/model or proposed system identification; b. Product literature, specification sheets, drawings, photographs, or other existing commercial literature describing the proposed system; c. A description showing how the proposed product meets each minimum technical requirement identified in Section 3; d. Identification of the number and types of training scenarios supported by the system; e. Description of construction materials and weather-resistant features; f. Description of forcible-entry, roof ventilation, second-story, confined-space, wall-breach, and entanglement capabilities; g. Statement identifying compliance with applicable NFPA 1402, NFPA 1006, and OSHA guardrail requirements; h. Proposed delivery lead time; and i. Warranty information. Merely restating the Government's requirements without providing supporting product information may be insufficient to demonstrate technical acceptability. DELIVERY Required Delivery: No later than ten (10) months after contract award. Earlier delivery is acceptable and encouraged. The Government's anticipated commercial lead time is approximately eight (8) to ten (10) months after contract award. Delivery Location: [INSERT COMPLETE DELIVERY LOCATION] Delivery shall be FOB Destination. The contractor shall coordinate the delivery date and time with the Government prior to shipment. The receiving activity will be responsible for offloading the training unit from the delivery vehicle. The Government will provide appropriate offloading equipment at the destination, including a forklift equipped with forks at least six (6) feet in length and having a minimum lifting capacity of 8,000 pounds. The contractor remains responsible for transportation and safe delivery of the unit to the designated delivery point. INSPECTION AND ACCEPTANCE Inspection and acceptance shall occur at destination. The Government will inspect the delivered item to verify that: a. The unit delivered is the item identified in the contractor's quotation; b. The unit conforms to the contract requirements; c. There is no apparent shipping or structural damage; d. Required components and accessories are present; and e. The unit is otherwise suitable for Government acceptance. Final payment shall be made following successful delivery, inspection, and Government acceptance in accordance with the applicable contract terms. WARRANTY The contractor shall provide its standard commercial warranty with its quotation. At a minimum: a. A structural warranty shall be provided for the primary training structure; b. Electronic enhancement equipment, when included, shall be covered by a minimum one-year warranty; and c. Safety lines, devices, or comparable safety components shall be covered by the manufacturer's applicable commercial warranty. Quoters shall clearly identify the duration, coverage, exclusions, and procedures associated with each warranty provided. QUOTATION REQUIREMENTS Quotations shall include, at a minimum: Company name and address; UEI; CAGE Code; Point of contact name, telephone number, and email address; Completed pricing for CLIN 0001; Total Firm-Fixed Price, including freight; Product make/model; Technical literature demonstrating compliance with the minimum requirements; Proposed delivery schedule; Warranty information; Quote validity period; Confirmation that the contractor is actively registered in SAM.gov; Any exceptions or deviations from the requirements of this solicitation; and A statement confirming that the quoted product meets or exceeds all minimum technical requirements. title: Projekt 1034: Technische Umsetzung einer SBOM für KI (SBOM4AI)
description: Im Bereich der klassischen Software finden Software Bills of Materials (SBOMs) – also Stücklisten, die Informationen über Softwarekomponenten und deren Abhängigkeiten beinhalten – schon lange Anwendung und werden vom Cyber Resilience Act (CRA) sogar gefordert. Diese Forderung gilt auch für KI-Systeme, jedoch ist die Idee einer SBOM spezifisch für KI-Systeme relativ neu. Erste Ansätze bergen daher die Gefahr, dass sie nicht alle notwendigen Aspekte im Hinblick auf die Transparenz der KI-Lieferkette abdecken. In diesem Projekt soll das im G7-Rahmen veröffentlichte Konzept "SBOM for AI - Minimum Elements" in die Praxis überführt und dafür eine technische Umsetzung der definierten Kriterien erarbeitet werden. Die SBOM für KI soll automatisiert erstellt und in einem geeigneten Format ausgegeben werden. Die erarbeitete Umsetzung soll anschließend allen Interessenträgern zur Verfügung gestellt werden, um so einen wichtigen Beitrag zur Cybersicherheit von KI-Systemen leisten zu können.

title: Cleaning Services for the Consulate of Canada to Germany, in Munich
description: The Consulate of Canada to Germany, in Munich hereinafter referred to the “Consulate” requires routine cleaning services for its office building (the Chancery). The work includes the provision of routine and periodic cleaning services, as well as any additional cleaning required to meet operational needs. Services must be provided in accordance with the specifications outlined in this Statement of Work and must support a clean, safe, and professional environment at all times while not interfering with the daily operations or activities of the Chancery’s occupants, clients, or visitors. The Consulate may also require very basic, unskilled services that would reasonably be within the capacity of a professional cleaner, such as shredding documents or watering plants. While the majority of the cleaning services will be performed at the Chancery on a daily basis, other cleaning services may be required on an as-and-when requested basis.

title: Analysis of the Beluga Fattening Cycle using photogrammetry
description: Fisheries and Oceans Canada (DFO) requires scientific expertise to assess the importance of spring in the annual fattening cycle of the endangered St. Lawrence Estuary beluga population. The work involves analyzing aerial drone imagery and morphometric data collected in 2024 and 2025 to evaluate seasonal changes in body condition among male, female, and pregnant belugas. The contractor will conduct advanced photogrammetric and morphometric analyses using image analysis software to refine sex identification, identify pregnant females, and assess changes in physical condition across age and sex classes. The work also includes the preparation and publication of two scientific articles that meet the standards of internationally recognized peer-reviewed scientific journals.

Hankinta koostuu seuraavista pääkokonaisuuksista: • Rekrytointijärjestelmä • Sijaisrekrytointijärjestelmä • Käyttöönottoprojekti, ml. pääkäyttäjien koulutukset & testaussuunnitelma • Tuki- ja ylläpitopalvelut • Koulutuskannan käyttömahdollisuus • Integraatiomahdollisuudet Tavoitteena on saada kaupungille luotettava ja käyttäjäystävällinen rekrytointijärjestelmä. Järjestelmän tulee tarjota myös sijaisten hallintaan ja koordinointiin käyttäjäystävällinen ja mahdollisimman automatisoitu alusta. Lisäksi järjestelmässä tulee olla hyvät ja tehokkaat raportointi- ja analytiikkaominaisuudet. Sopimuskauden on tarkoitus alkaa helmikuusta 2028. title: EPX-55555-000 � 96-Well Hand-Held Magnetic Plate Washer and EPX480-20834-901 � MO Immune Monitoring 48Plex, 96 Tests
description: NOTICE OF INTENT � SOLE SOURCE ACQUISITION Notice No.: 75N98026Q01254 The National Institutes of Health (NIH) intends to award a Firm-Fixed-Price Purchase Order to Thermo Fisher Scientific for the following products: EPX-55555-000 � 96-Well Hand-Held Magnetic Plate Washer EPX480-20834-901 � MO Immune Monitoring 48Plex, 96 Tests The Government intends to solicit from a single source in accordance with FAR 6.302-1, Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements. DESCRIPTION OF REQUIREMENT The research project is investigating the effects of sarcoma cancers and autoimmune disease on ovarian function in humans. A principal objective of the research is to determine whether alterations in pro-inflammatory signaling are associated with impaired or altered ovarian function. The research requires measurement of concentrations of multiple soluble inflammatory markers in biological specimens, including blood and ovarian tissue. The requested ProcartaPlex MO Immune Monitoring 48Plex assay provides simultaneous measurement of 48 soluble immune-related markers using a multiplex bead-based assay platform. The requirement consists of the following: EPX480-20834-901 � MO Immune Monitoring 48Plex, 96 Tests, for multiplex measurement of the required 48 soluble immune and inflammatory markers; and EPX-55555-000 � 96-Well Hand-Held Magnetic Plate Washer, required to support the magnetic-bead assay processing and washing steps associated with the multiplex assay workflow. The requested supplies are necessary to complete the laboratory analysis of biological specimens already generated during the research study. JUSTIFICATION FOR SOLE-SOURCE ACQUISITION The requested ProcartaPlex assay is required because the research protocol calls for simultaneous measurement of a defined panel of 48 soluble immune and inflammatory markers from the study specimens. The assay provides the required multiplex capability and is configured to permit the research team to evaluate a broad panel of inflammatory biomarkers from limited biological sample volumes. The research involves specimens obtained from an animal study in which the animals have already been euthanized and the biological specimens have been collected. These specimens represent a finite research resource and cannot readily be recreated without repeating the underlying animal study. Failure to obtain and analyze the available specimens would prevent the investigators from completing the planned biomarker analysis and would materially limit the ability to compare the animal findings with the corresponding human research. The requested Thermo Fisher products are required to maintain consistency with the assay methodology, reagents, plate format, detection technology, and established laboratory procedures being used for this research. Substitution with a different assay platform would require development, validation, and/or re-optimization of an alternative 48-marker panel and could introduce differences in assay chemistry, sensitivity, specificity, calibration, dynamic range, and reported concentrations. Such differences could compromise the comparability of results generated from the existing specimens and the ability to relate the experimental findings to the corresponding human research. The EPX480-20834-901 ProcartaPlex MO Immune Monitoring 48Plex is therefore required to obtain the specified 48-plex biomarker measurements. The EPX-55555-000 96-Well Hand-Held Magnetic Plate Washer is required to support the magnetic-bead washing steps associated with the multiplex assay workflow and to provide consistent processing of the assay plates. Because the research specimens are limited and cannot readily be replaced, use of a different analytical platform would create a risk that the specimens could be consumed during method development, optimization, or validation without producing data directly comparable to the required assay results. The Government is seeking sources capable of providing the exact required products and satisfying all of the Government's technical requirements. Based on the requiring activity's technical assessment, the requested Thermo Fisher products are believed to be the only supplies that satisfy the Government's specific research requirements without requiring development and validation of an alternative analytical methodology. RESPONSE INFORMATION This notice is not a request for competitive quotations or proposals. However, interested parties that believe they can satisfy the Government's requirements may submit a capability statement demonstrating their ability to provide the required products and satisfy all specified technical and operational requirements. Capability statements should include sufficient technical information to demonstrate the firm's ability to provide: EPX-55555-000 � 96-Well Hand-Held Magnetic Plate Washer; and EPX480-20834-901 � MO Immune Monitoring 48Plex, 96 Tests; or otherwise demonstrate the firm's ability to provide products that meet all of the Government's stated minimum technical requirements. description: NON-COMPETITIVE COMBINED SYNOPSIS / SOLICITATION 7571PS26Q00130 Title: NIH-wide Doctoral Partnership Training Program �University of Oxford (i) This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the format in part 12 as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; proposals are being requested and a written solicitation will not be issued. The Solicitation number is 7571PS26Q00130 issued as a Request for Quotation to support the Doctoral Partnership Training Program at the University of Oxford. This solicitation incorporates provisions and clauses by reference. The full text of provisions and clauses may be accessed electronically at www.acquisition.gov. The Defense Priorities and Allocations System (DPAS) are not applicable to this requirement. THIS IS A NON-COMPETITIVE (NOTICE OF INTENT) COMBINED SYNOPSIS SOLICITATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT OR PURCHASE ORDER WITHOUT PROVIDING FOR FULL OR OPEN COMPETITION (INCLUDING BRAND-NAME). The Office of Mission Acquisition Solutions (OMAS), Office of Acquisitions (OA), on behalf of The National Institute on Allergy Infectious Diseases (NIAID), intends to negotiate and award a purchase order without providing for full and open competition (including brand-name) to University of Oxford, University Offices, Wellington Square, Oxford, Oxfordshire, OX1 2JD, United Kingdom for the NIH Fellows roster. This acquisition is conducted as non-competitive for a commercial product or commercial service and is conducted pursuant to FAR Subpart 12.201-1�Simplified Procedures, in accordance with 41 United States Code (U.S.C.) 1901 Simplified acquisition procedures Pursuant to FAR subpart 12.102(b) Restricting Competition, in accordance with FAR 6.103-1(b) (ii) This requirement is for the following services: The National Institutes of Health (NIH) Division of Medical Sciences, the University of Oxofrd of the United Kingdom, and the NIH-wide Global Doctoral Partnership (NGDP) Program have a shared interest in fostering collaborative research. The NIH provides, through its offices and investigators, the recruitment of exceptional students from the United States who will carry out graduate-level training and research for the 2025-2026 academic year under coordinated mentors at the NIH and University of Oxford. This acquisition seeks to cover the tuition fees for both new (incoming) and continuing students in the program for the 2025-2026 academic year. The program of study shall include co-supervision for trainees at the University and the NIH. Basic and applied research shall be carried out by the trainees at both institutions. Only this suggested source can furnish the requirements: University of Oxford University Offices Wellington Square Oxford, Oxfordshire, OX1 2JD United Kingdom (iii) Description of requirement: The University of Oxford shall provide 36 graduate-level training and research for students for the 2026-2027 academic year. In addition to administrative oversight, the University shall provide for the following functions: Shared core values (NIH and University) Advance the NIH mission of global outreach and training by contributing internationally collaborative research in areas of emerging and infectious disease, global health, and international medicine. Common government pursuit of public health care and health care initiatives. University requirements The partnering University must have a tutorial system where faculty fellows teach students in groups of one to three on a weekly basis. The tutorial system is uniquely required for the student training in the International PhD Program because there is no formal didactic component required for degree completion. The tutorial system will allow students to receive direct feedback on their NIH projects. It will also provide an opportunity to discuss the published literature and to learn how to think critically like a scientist. University provides access to classes for students virtually online or safely in-person. Shared training between the NIH and the University. Students spend a maximum of two years at the partner institution. The remaining two years of PhD experiential work must be spent at the NIH. Demonstrated emphasis on quality research with supplemental coursework and skills enrichment opportunities available but not mandatory. The students in the graduate partnership program work collaboratively in any one of the 27 Institutes and centers that make up the NIH. These include but not limited to: NCI-CCR, NCI-DCEG, NEI, NHGRI, NHLBI, NIA, NIAAA, NIAID, NIAMS, NICHD, NIDA, NIDCD, NIDCR, NIDDK, NIMH, NINDS, NLM, VRC, NCATS, CIT, NIEHS, CC. The degree conferring institution that partners with the NIH must have a pool of researchers that the research expertise found at the NIH. The partnering institution must have various schools and program that are available as training environments (centers). Demonstrated evidence of academic history of scientific research and training spanning seven to eight centuries. Common requirements for mentorship and training of graduate students. Demonstrated performance: evidence of students who have successfully completed doctoral degrees through a partnership-training program. Abundant opportunities to form collaborations between Principal Investigators based on common program missions and shared biomedical interests in global health and medicine. Existing network of published principal investigators. Common access to contemporary and technologically advanced research facilities. Opportunity for international collaboration and intellectual transfer without language barriers. English must be spoken exclusively in NIH laboratories. Infrastructure and staff dedicated to international training collaborations. Research specialties in infectious disease, cancer, immunology, neurology, vaccine research, genomics, child health, and human development. Clinical aspect integrated into graduate training with hospitals located on University campus. Administrative oversight Supervision of existing student participants who have been accepted into the NIH Oxford-Cambridge Scholars Program and who are continuing training for the 2025-2026 academic scholastic year. The 2026 scholastic enrollment of existing students shall consist of multiple participants. Reviewing University application packages for matriculating students to ensure that all admission documents have been received, reviewed, and validated. Informing students of Visa requirements. Notifying student program participants of his/her acceptance to the university and college. Provision of research opportunities in university laboratories with qualified faculty members who will serve as mentors and advisors to the students in the program. Participation and support of annual research colloquia and other program activities. Facilitation of the entry of U.S. students into the full college life of the University as members of the Colleges at the University. Provision of University housing for students in the program. title: Relocation of the Nano and Micro HPLC Systems and the Q Exactive Mass Spectrometer.
description: NOTICE OF INTENT � SOLE SOURCE ACQUISITION Notice No.: 75N98026Q01253 The National Institutes of Health (NIH) intends to award a Firm-Fixed-Price Purchase Order to Thermo Electron for the relocation of the Nano and Micro HPLC Systems and the Q Exactive Mass Spectrometer. The Government intends to solicit from a single source in accordance with FAR 6.302-1, Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements. Description of Requirement The objective of this requirement is to safely relocate the Government's Nano HPLC System, Micro HPLC System, and Q Exactive Mass Spectrometer from a radiochemistry laboratory in Building 10 to the Mass Spectrometry Unit in Building 13. The instruments require specialized disassembly, packaging, transportation preparation, reassembly, and post-relocation diagnostic testing. The relocation must be performed in a manner that protects the instruments from damage and ensures that they remain properly configured and operational following installation at the new location. The required services include, but are not limited to, the following: Provide instrument-specific shipping crates designed and/or approved for the Nano HPLC System, Micro HPLC System, and Q Exactive Mass Spectrometer. Disassemble the Nano HPLC System, Micro HPLC System, and Q Exactive Mass Spectrometer at the Building 10 laboratory. Properly secure and package each instrument in the appropriate instrument-specific crate in preparation for relocation. Provide the technical expertise necessary to safely prepare the instruments for transport. Reassemble and install the instruments at the Building 13 Mass Spectrometry Unit. Perform diagnostic testing and appropriate operational checks following reassembly to verify that the Nano HPLC System, Micro HPLC System, and Q Exactive Mass Spectrometer are functioning properly. Address any installation-related issues identified during post-relocation diagnostic testing. Justification for Sole-Source Acquisition The Government has determined that Thermo Electron is the only known source capable of providing the required relocation services while maintaining the technical and operational integrity of the instruments. The instruments are Thermo Electron-manufactured systems that require specialized knowledge of their configuration, components, connections, disassembly procedures, reassembly procedures, and manufacturer-specific diagnostic requirements. The relocation involves more than ordinary equipment moving services and requires qualified technical personnel capable of disassembling and reassembling the systems without compromising their performance or configuration. The requirement also includes instrument-specific crates designed to protect the Nano HPLC System, Micro HPLC System, and Q Exactive Mass Spectrometer during relocation. The Government requires that the instruments be properly disassembled, secured, transported, reassembled, and diagnostically tested by personnel possessing the necessary technical knowledge and experience with these systems. Use of a general laboratory equipment moving service or an otherwise unqualified third party could introduce a risk of damage, improper reassembly, loss of instrument configuration, or failure to restore the systems to operational status. Such risks could result in additional costs, equipment downtime, and delays to ongoing research activities. Based on the Government's market research and knowledge of the equipment, Thermo Electron possesses the specialized technical expertise and manufacturer-specific knowledge necessary to perform the complete relocation, reassembly, and diagnostic testing of these instruments. Accordingly, the Government believes that Thermo Electron is the only responsible source capable of satisfying the requirement without unacceptable risk to the equipment and associated research operations. Response Information This notice is not a request for competitive quotations. However, interested parties that believe they can meet the Government's requirements may submit a capability statement demonstrating their ability to provide the required services and satisfy all specified technical and operational requirements. Capability statements must specifically address the offeror's: Experience disassembling and reassembling Thermo Electron Nano and Micro HPLC systems and Q Exactive Mass Spectrometers; Availability of qualified technicians with manufacturer-specific training or equivalent documented technical qualifications; Ability to provide appropriate instrument-specific crates or equivalent manufacturer-approved protective packaging; Ability to safely prepare the instruments for transport and reassemble them at the destination laboratory; and Ability to perform post-installation diagnostic and operational testing. The Government will consider all timely capability statements received and will determine whether the acquisition should proceed as a sole-source procurement or be competed. The Government anticipates making an award approximately one (1) calendar day after the closing date of this notice, unless the Government determines that another responsible source is capable of meeting the requirement. Capability statements shall be submitted electronically to haunp@mail.nih.gov no later than 9:00 a.m. EDT on September 28, 2026. Please reference Notice No. 75N98026Q01253 in the subject line of the response.

description: NON-COMPETITIVE COMBINED SYNOPSIS / SOLICITATION 7571PS26Q00128 Title: NIH-wide Doctoral Partnership Training Program - University of Cambridge (i) This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the format in part 12 as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; proposals are being requested and a written solicitation will not be issued. The Solicitation number is 7571PS26Q00128 issued as a Request for Quotation to support the Doctoral Partnership Training Program at the University of Cambridge. This solicitation incorporates provisions and clauses by reference. The full text of provisions and clauses may be accessed electronically at www.acquisition.gov. The Defense Priorities and Allocations System (DPAS) are not applicable to this requirement. THIS IS A NON-COMPETITIVE (NOTICE OF INTENT) COMBINED SYNOPSIS SOLICITATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT OR PURCHASE ORDER WITHOUT PROVIDING FOR FULL OR OPEN COMPETITION (INCLUDING BRAND-NAME). The Office of Mission Acquisition Solutions (OMAS), Office of Acquisitions (OA), on behalf of The National Institute on Allergy Infectious Diseases (NIAID), intends to negotiate and award a purchase order without providing for full and open competition (including brand-name) to University of Cambridge, Research Operations Office, Greenwich House, Madingley Road, Cambridge CB3-0TX, United Kingdom for the NIH Fellows roster. This acquisition is conducted as non-competitive for a commercial product or commercial service and is conducted pursuant to FAR Subpart 12.201-1�Simplified Procedures, in accordance with 41 United States Code (U.S.C.) 1901 Simplified acquisition procedures Pursuant to FAR subpart 12.102(b) Restricting Competition, in accordance with FAR 6.103-1(b) (ii) This requirement is for the following services: The National Institutes of Health (NIH) Division of Medical Sciences, the University of Cambridge of the United Kingdom, and the NIH-wide Global Doctoral Partnership (NGDP) Program have a shared interest in fostering collaborative research. The NIH provides, through its offices and investigators, the recruitment of exceptional students from the United States who will carry out graduate-level training and research for the 2025-2026 academic year under coordinated mentors at the NIH and University of Cambridge. This acquisition seeks to cover the tuition fees for both new (incoming) and continuing students in the program for the 2025-2026 academic year. The program of study shall include co-supervision for trainees at the University and the NIH. Basic and applied research shall be carried out by the trainees at both institutions. Only this suggested source can furnish the requirements: University of Cambridge Research Operations Office Greenwich House Madingley Road Cambridge CB3 0TX UNITED KINGDOM (iii) Description of requirement: The University of Cambridge shall provide 33 graduate-level training and research for students for the 2026-2027 academic year. In addition to administrative oversight, the University shall provide for the following functions: Shared core values (NIH and University) Advance the NIH mission of global outreach and training by contributing internationally collaborative research in areas of emerging and infectious disease, global health, and international medicine. Common government pursuit of public health care and health care initiatives. University requirements The partnering University must have a tutorial system where faculty fellows teach students in groups of one to three on a weekly basis. The tutorial system is uniquely required for the student training in the International PhD Program because there is no formal didactic component required for degree completion. The tutorial system will allow students to receive direct feedback on their NIH projects. It will also provide an opportunity to discuss the published literature and to learn how to think critically like a scientist. University provides access to classes for students virtually online or safely in-person. Shared training between the NIH and the University. Students spend a maximum of two years at the partner institution. The remaining two years of PhD experiential work must be spent at the NIH. Demonstrated emphasis on quality research with supplemental coursework and skills enrichment opportunities available but not mandatory. The students in the graduate partnership program work collaboratively in any one of the 27 Institutes and centers that make up the NIH. These include but not limited to: NCI-CCR, NCI-DCEG, NEI, NHGRI, NHLBI, NIA, NIAAA, NIAID, NIAMS, NICHD, NIDA, NIDCD, NIDCR, NIDDK, NIMH, NINDS, NLM, VRC, NCATS, CIT, NIEHS, CC. The degree conferring institution that partners with the NIH must have a pool of researchers that the research expertise found at the NIH. The partnering institution must have various schools and program that are available as training environments (centers). Demonstrated evidence of academic history of scientific research and training spanning seven to eight centuries. Common requirements for mentorship and training of graduate students. Demonstrated performance: evidence of students who have successfully completed doctoral degrees through a partnership-training program. Abundant opportunities to form collaborations between Principal Investigators based on common program missions and shared biomedical interests in global health and medicine. Existing network of published principal investigators. Common access to contemporary and technologically advanced research facilities. Opportunity for international collaboration and intellectual transfer without language barriers. English must be spoken exclusively in NIH laboratories. Infrastructure and staff dedicated to international training collaborations. Research specialties in infectious disease, cancer, immunology, neurology, vaccine research, genomics, child health, and human development. Clinical aspect integrated into graduate training with hospitals located on University campus. Administrative oversight Supervision of existing student participants who have been accepted into the NIH Oxford-Cambridge Scholars Program and who are continuing training for the 2025-2026 academic scholastic year. The 2026 scholastic enrollment of existing students shall consist of multiple participants. Reviewing University application packages for matriculating students to ensure that all admission documents have been received, reviewed, and validated. Informing students of Visa requirements. Notifying student program participants of his/her acceptance to the university and college. Provision of research opportunities in university laboratories with qualified faculty members who will serve as mentors and advisors to the students in the program. Participation and support of annual research colloquia and other program activities. Facilitation of the entry of U.S. students into the full college life of the University as members of the Colleges at the University. Provision of University housing for students in the program. (iv) The Government anticipates award of a firm fixed-price purchase order for this acquisition, and the anticipated period of performance will begin on or around 09/30/2026 through 09/29/2027 for one year. Finland – Air sanitisers – Ilmanpuhdistuslaitteiden vuokraus ja hankinta
description: Vantaan kaupunki pyytää tarjouksia ilmanpuhdistimien vuokraamisesta ja hankinnasta. Hankinnan kohteena ovat vuokrattavat ja ostettavat sisäilmanpuhdistuslaitteet julkisiin tiloihin, kuten koulu- ja päiväkotitiloihin, toimistoihin, arkistoihin, auditorioihin jne. Tilaajat hankkivat pääosin vuokrattavia laitteita, ja vähäisissä määrin laitteita tullaan ostamaan omaksi. Ilmanpuhdistimilla haetaan väliaikaista ratkaisua sisäilmaongelmien hallintaan käyttöä turvaavana toimenpiteenä. Ilmanpuhdistimien tulee olla tarkoitettu tähän käyttötarkoitukseen. Hankinnan kohde on kuvattu tarkemmin tarjouspyynnön liitteellä 2 Palvelukuvaus. Kilpailutus suoritetaan avoimella menettelyllä, jonka perusteella jokaiseen osa-alueeseen puitetoimittajiksi valitaan kolme (3) vertailussa eniten pisteitä saanutta tarjoajaa etusijajärjestyksessä. Hankinta kilpailutetaan yhteishankintana niin, että Vantaan kaupunki julkaisee tarjouspyynnön. Kilpailutuksen perusteella tehdään samansisältöiset, sopimusluonnoksen (liite 1) mukaiset sopimukset Vantaan kaupungille, Kauniaisten kaupungille ja Vantaan ja Keravan hyvinvointialueelle. Hankintayksiköt tekevät myös oman päätöksensä. Vantaan kaupungille tehtävien sopimusten perusteella hankintoja voivat tehdä Vantaan kaupungin kaikki toimialat sekä Vantaan Tilapalvelut Vantti Oy, VTK Kiinteistöt Oy- konserni, VAV Yhtymä Oy, VAV Asunnot Oy, VAV Palvelukodit Oy, VAV Hoiva-asunnot Oy, Hakopolun Liikekiinteistö Oy, Kiinteistö Oy Hakucenter, Kiinteistö Oy Vantaan Maakotkantie 10, Pallastunturintien Liikekiinteistö Oy ja Asunto Oy Vantaan Katriinanrinne. Sopimustoimittaja voi tarjota samoin ehdoin tuotteitaan ja palvelujaan Vantaan kaupungin seuraaville konsernitoimijoille: Vivamus Kiinteistöt Oy ja Kiinteistö Oy Vantaan Sote-tilat. Sopimuskausi on kaksi (2) vuotta, jonka jälkeen sopimusta voidaan jatkaa kahdella (2) yhden (1) vuoden optiolla (1+1). Hankintayksikkö ei sitoudu tarjouspyyntöasiakirjoissa ilmoitettuihin euromääräisiin arvoihin tai tiettyihin arvioituihin hankintamääriin sopimuskaudella.

title: Reintegration Services and Indigenous Community Support
description: An advanced contract award notice (ACAN) is a public notice indicating to the supplier community that a department or agency intends to award a contract for goods, services or construction to a pre-identified supplier, thereby allowing other suppliers to signal their interest in bidding, by submitting a statement of capabilities. If no supplier submits a statement of capabilities that meets the requirements set out in the ACAN, on or before the closing date and time stated in the ACAN, the contracting officer may then proceed with the award to the pre-identified supplier. 1. Definition of the requirement: Policy on Reciprocal Procurement: the Policy on Reciprocal Procurement does not apply to this procurement. The Correctional Service of Canada has a requirement to provide in person support and assistance to Indigenous offenders to help them enter the workforce, including real-life, day to day mentorship and job preparedness development. The work will involve the following: 1.1 Objectives: The Contractor must provide reintegrative supports to Indigenous offenders, including First Nations, Métis and Inuit, such as Elder support, cultural teachings, counselling and hard and soft employability skills. The Contractor must provide jobsite support and engage with Indigenous offenders to check on morale, workmanship, and identify whether issues that may be arising that require intervention. 1.2 Tasks: The Contractor must provide reintegration and transition support services and interventions through job training including but not limited to: 1. Identifying and triaging, based on need and release dates, Indigenous offenders who require support for release planning. This includes but is not limited to, those who are under CSC custody with a release occurring during the period of the contract and are participating in CSC CORCAN and Pathways initiatives. 2. Providing continuous reintegration services to offenders under the Contractor’s care up to the offenders’ warrant expiry date (WED). 3. Providing in-person visits to Stony Mountain Institution’s minimum-security units as well as visits to the medium and maximum units according to an agreed schedule with CSC, to provide information and identify any Indigenous offenders who require support in the areas that the Contractor can provide. 4. Providing their training program to offenders. 5. Entering eligible offenders into the trainee pool for future employment. 6. Providing in class job training for offenders that demonstrate a need in that domain. 7. Providing job mentorship to offenders. 8. Providing in person support to offenders on the job site to check on morale, workmanship, and to identify issues requiring intervention by the Contractor support team. 9. Offering sweat lodges to offenders once every seven weeks. 10. Offering cultural teachings and engagement with staff through the Contractor’s Knowledge Keeper including lived experience and traditional teachings with the support of a Care Planner responsible for reintegration. 11. Providing on-demand counselling services through the Knowledge Keeper and Care Planner. 12. Offering wrap-around supports including, but not limited to case management, Elder support, cultural teaching, counselling, and skills that will assist them in the labour and trade field. 13. Offering wrap-around support through its training and support department including, but not limited to, housing support, healthy relationship teachings, money management. 14. title: Building Envelope Construction Services for Various International Locations.
description: The Department of Foreign Affairs, Trade and Development Canada (DFATD) operates around 189 missions abroad to provide services to Canadians and to maintain diplomatic relationships with host countries. As part of these missions, DFATD occupies a portfolio of buildings requiring the delivery of operations & maintenance (O&M) services to maintain the integrity of the assets. In managing these assets, DFATD is required to complete construction projects of various sizes, and to perform O&M work. title: Generator Rental Services for the Embassy of Canada to Haiti, in Port-au-Prince
description: The Department of Foreign Affairs, Trade and Development intends to establish a contract for the rental of five (5) diesel generators to provide the primary electrical power supply for certain facilities of the Embassy of Canada in Port-au-Prince, Haiti, including the chancery, the official residence and employee residences. The requirement is for a turnkey solution that includes, but is not limited to, the supply, delivery, installation, commissioning, operation, maintenance and removal of the generators at the end of the Contract. Depending on the specific needs of the different facilities, the services also include the supply of fuel and the installation, operation and maintenance of the equipment required for its storage, transfer and filtration, and for supplying fuel to the generators. The Contractor will be responsible for providing all qualified personnel, equipment, materials, tools, replacement parts and related services required to ensure the continuous and safe operation of the systems. The Contractor must also provide preventive and corrective maintenance, emergency support available at all times, and the prompt replacement of any equipment that cannot be returned to service within the prescribed timeframes. All Work must be performed in accordance with the applicable codes, standards, safety requirements and manufacturers’ recommendations.

title: Air Bath for Standard Resistors
description: An air bath for standard resistors is a temperature-controlled enclosure that maintains precision resistance standards at a stable and uniform temperature. Since the resistance value of standard resistors is temperature dependent, tight temperature control is essential for accurate resistance measurements used in thermometry applications such as standard platinum resistance thermometer calibrations. The laboratory is acquiring an air bath to replace the current oil bath system. Compared to oil baths, air baths provide cleaner operation, lower maintenance, no risk of oil contamination or leakage, and easier handling of resistors and wiring, while maintaining excellent temperature stability for precision measurements.

title: Geographic Information System Data Architect
description: This bid solicitation is being issued to satisfy the requirement of one (1) G.5 Geographic Information System Data Architect, Level 3 for Housing, Infrastructure and Communities Canada for Task-Based Informatics Professional Services (TBIPS) under the TBIPS Supply Arrangement (SA) method of supply. The primary objective is to establish a centralized geospatial data environment within the organization’s Azure-based Unified Data Platform (UDP). This environment will enable the efficient ingestion, validation, storage, integration, sharing, and spatial analysis of geospatial data across the organization, while supporting real-time relationships between spatial data and enterprise business datasets, automation, and more consistent, data-driven decision-making. In addition, the organization is looking for a cost-benefit analysis and recommendation of options to procure a modern geospatial platform, including how these options compare and integrate with HICC’s existing spatial capabilities and data ecosystems. The analysis will assess the potential value, costs, and implementation considerations associated with these platforms, and identify opportunities for location-based analysis, research, reporting, evaluation, automation, and application geoprocessing capabilities across the department.

description: NOTICE OF PROPOSED PROCUREMENT (NPP) The Department of National Defence (DND), in support of the Canadian Forces Health Services (CFHS), has a requirement for the supply, delivery, installation, testing, commissioning, documentation, and warranty support of ten (10) Mobile Treatment Centre (MTC) cap-style slide-in modules.
